utility.notes: The greater Truckee area has been served by the publicly-owned Truckee Donner Public Utility District (established 1927) since its founding, confirmed via TDPUD's own site and its membership in the Northern California Power Agency (NCPA). This is a public utility district, not PG&E, independently confirmed rather than assumed from county location.

value.name: Truckee Donner Public Utility District (TDPUD)
value.notes: TDPUD is a public utility district (not an IOU-served city), so it is structurally outside CCA enrollment the same way other municipal/public utility districts in this dataset are (e.g. Alameda Municipal Power, Gridley Electric Utility, Lompoc Utilities): a CCA only replaces the default generation of an underlying investor-owned utility's (PG&E/SCE/SDG&E) customers, and TDPUD customers are never IOU customers to begin with. Pioneer Community Energy's own homepage (directly re-verified this session) also confirms its current service area is limited to specific Placer/El Dorado County communities and does not include Truckee. TDPUD is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

county.notes: Truckee straddles Nevada and Placer Counties; its Town Hall and primary municipal seat are in Nevada County.

permit_authority.value: Town of Truckee Community Development Department, Building Division

interconnection_url.notes: TDPUD's own current Solar/Wind/Battery Interconnections page (the earlier URL found via search-engine indexing was dead; this current URL was located and directly verified this session). As a public utility district, TDPUD runs its own interconnection review/approval process rather than a statewide IOU NEM program.

battery_programs.notes: Battery storage systems are covered under the same Symbium-based residential solar and battery storage permitting process, but this is a permitting-pathway detail rather than a distinct incentive/rebate battery program.

value.name: Site, roof layout, electrical, and mounting plans

value: Post-installation requires a solar assessment report from a CEC-approved tool, plus photographic documentation confirming the installed system matches the modeled design (Town of Truckee building permit requirement)

Separately, following construction, a TDPUD electrician conducts a site inspection to ensure the interconnection installation meets standards before the system may be energized (TDPUD Interconnection Agreement requirement)

other_conditions: Systems must comply with the 2025 California Residential Code (Sections R324 and R907), the 2022 California Electrical Code, and Truckee's own Design Guidelines and Criteria
TDPUD must separately review and approve all solar/battery projects for electrical safety and grid reliability

value.name: Symbium processing fee
value.unit: paid to Symbium at submission, separate from the Town permit fee
value.notes: The Town permit fee is billed separately to the applicant afterward. Exception reviews are billed hourly (1-hour minimum).

value.name: TDPUD Interconnection Agreement Fee
value.notes: Per TDPUD's own Solar/Wind/Battery Interconnections page, this is separate from and in addition to the Town of Truckee's own building permit fee.

value.role: Town of Truckee Community Development Department
